destructive_ablation.destructive_interpretation: B - C = +13.2pp: active interrogation DOES add value beyond passive ML (≥10pp threshold met). ML only helps if you DON'T have active perturbation (C=42.1% vs A=55.8%). DESTRUCTIVE FINDING: The 'ML + active' combination (Family D proposal) is NOT buyer-grade. Active interrogation alone (threshold) is sufficient. ML adds complexity without benefit.

position_2_selective_retention.core_mechanism: size-selective filtration element in shunt lumen: permits CSF, retains therapeutic

destructive_test.question: Does hydrogel solve the SAME coupled problem: selective retention WHILE preserving clinically adequate CSF drainage?
destructive_test.hydrogel_paper: Intrathecal delivery of a polymeric nanocomposite hydrogel after spinal cord injury (2010, Biomaterials, cited 164)
destructive_test.hydrogel_2014_followup: Sustained delivery of bioactive neurotrophin-3 to the injured spinal cord (2014)
hydrogel_architecture: Injectable DDS (drug depot injected into intrathecal space)
Biodegradable polymeric nanoparticles in hyaluronan/methyl cellulose hydrogel
Sustained release for 28-50 days (depot mechanism, NOT filtration)
Application: spinal cord injury (NOT CSF drainage / hydrocephalus)
NO integration into a shunt lumen
destructive_test.destructive_verdict: Hydrogel does NOT solve the coupled problem. It is a SUSTAINED RELEASE DEPOT, not a SELECTIVE FILTRATION ELEMENT. It does not preserve CSF drainage (it's a drug depot, not a flow element). It is architecturally DIFFERENT — different mechanism (depot vs filter), different application (SCI vs CSF drainage), different constraint (no drainage requirement). Position #2's coupled problem (retention + drainage) is NOT solved by hydrogel.

position_3_therapeutic_retention.core_mechanism: deliver therapeutic to CSF via shunt + selectively retain + maintain drainage

destructive_test.question: Does any cited literature teach therapeutic retention WHILE maintaining drainage function?
literature_reviewed: Methotrexate ICV delivery (1975, cited 611) — ICV injection, no retention mechanism, no simultaneous drainage
ICV insulin infusion (1979, cited 904) — chronic ICV infusion, no retention, no drainage preservation
Antisense oligonucleotide intrathecal (2013, cited 580) — modern intrathecal delivery, no retention-while-draining
CSF hydrodynamics review (2011, cited 207) — acknowledges drainage importance, does not propose retention
Choroidal blood-CSF barrier (2018, cited 368) — biological barrier research, not implantable retention
destructive_test.destructive_verdict: NO cited literature teaches therapeutic retention WHILE maintaining drainage function. All historical ICV/intrathecal delivery approaches use INJECTION or INFUSION — they do not simultaneously DRAIN CSF. The coupled problem (retention + drainage) is NOT taught. Position #3's flagship claim A (retention while draining) SURVIVES the destructive test.

engineering_status.verdict: VALIDATED — Position #3's coupled problem is NOT solved by any cited literature.
